definitions.explanation: In mathematics, one of the whole, non-negative counting numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on. In most Japanese school textbooks the set starts from 1, though some advanced or international treatments include 0. A technical term used in math class and any writing about arithmetic, number theory, or logic.

examples.japanese: {自然数|しぜんすう}の{集合|しゅうごう}は{無限|むげん}だ。
examples.english: The set of natural numbers is infinite.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}では{最初|さいしょ}に{自然数|しぜんすう}の{計算|けいさん}を{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: In elementary school, students first learn arithmetic with natural numbers.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{数学|すうがく}の{教科書|きょうかしょ}では、{自然数|しぜんすう}は{一般|いっぱん}{的|てき}に1から{始|はじ}まる{正|せい}の{整数|せいすう}と{定義|ていぎ}されている。
examples.english: In Japanese math textbooks, natural numbers are generally defined as the positive integers starting from 1.

notes:
Composed of {自然|しぜん} (natural) + {数|すう} (number). A direct translation of the mathematical term 'natural number.' The everyday word {自然|しぜん} ('nature') is not the intuition behind this use — {自然数|しぜんすう} refers specifically to the 'naturally occurring' counting numbers that any child begins with: 1, 2, 3, and so on.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自然数|しぜんすう}の{集合|しゅうごう}: the set of natural numbers
- {自然数|しぜんすう}の{和|わ}: the sum of natural numbers
- {自然数|しぜんすう}の{積|せき}: the product of natural numbers
- {正|せい}の{自然数|しぜんすう}: positive natural numbers
- {任意|にんい}の{自然数|しぜんすう}: any natural number / an arbitrary natural number
- {自然数|しぜんすう}{列|れつ}: a sequence of natural numbers

RELATED NUMBER TYPES:
- {整数|せいすう}: integer — includes 0 and negatives (..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ...).
- {正|せい}の{整数|せいすう}: positive integer — in Japanese school math, usually equivalent to {自然数|しぜんすう}.
- {有理数|ゆうりすう}: rational number — any number expressible as p/q.
- {無理数|むりすう}: irrational number.
- {実数|じっすう}: real number.
- {虚数|きょすう}: imaginary number.
- {複素数|ふくそすう}: complex number.
- {素数|そすう}: prime number.

USAGE NOTE:
Whether {自然数|しぜんすう} includes 0 is a point of divergence between traditions. Japanese high-school and college entrance exams generally treat {自然数|しぜんすう} as starting from 1; university-level set theory and computer science, influenced by ISO and Bourbaki conventions, often include 0. When writing or reading a math problem, always check how the text defines the term.

REGISTER:
A technical term from mathematics. It has no casual uses, but it is basic vocabulary that every Japanese schoolchild meets early.
